name: Unbounded completeness criterion
definition: A criterion asks for a complete or exhaustive result over a set with no bounded method or stopping rule, or the criterion's scope differs from the scope of the instruction it checks.
question_template: What finite check would let a reviewer say yes to this criterion, and when does it stop? Do the instruction line and the criterion cover the same set?
severity_guidance: Blocking when the criterion can never be shown true, so every review round can add one more item; minor when only the wording is loose.
known_weakness: A set word with no bound that the model must judge as bounded elsewhere; contradicting tasks are not scripted; the evidence is symptom-level.
